items.title: Localisations of an absolutely integrally closed ring are strictly henselian
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that the local ring of an absolutely integrally closed ring at a prime is strictly henselian. The proof first reduces, using the behaviour of the property under quotients and localisations, to the case where the ring is local and the prime is its maximal ideal. There the residue field is algebraically closed by the same reduction, and every monic polynomial over the ring decomposes completely into linear factors, which is precisely the condition in the definition of a henselian (indeed strictly henselian) ring, so the definition applies directly.
